15583017_0e0205b2.text: Orexins (orexin-A and -B) are neuropeptides expressed exclusively by neurons in the lateral hypothalamic area (LHA)

15583017_a826e725.text: Although the number of orexin neurons is small (approximately 4,000 cells in the mouse brain), these neurons project axons throughout the central nervous system (Peyron et al., 1998)( ��, 2007) and consequently affect various homeostatic functions. Dense projections from orexin neurons are observed in the serotonergic dorsal raphe nucleus (DR), noradrenergic locus coeruleus (LC), and histaminergic tuberomammillary nucleus (TMN), and all of these nuclei are involved in promoting arousal (Saper et al., 2005)

15583017_aec21329.text: anatomical studies of neural networks and analyses of transgenic mice have revealed integrated roles for orexin neurons in the coordination of emotion, energy homeostasis, and the reward system. A functional link between the limbic system and orexin neurons may be important for increasing vigilance in response to emotional stimuli. These findings suggest that orexin neurons relay information about an organism’s environment to maintain the proper amount of sleep and wakefulness in animals.
